company.name: Orlenby Family Medicine
company.blurb: An independent primary care practice in one office: five physicians, one of them the owner, with medical assistants, a front desk team, billing and a referral coordinator: 20 people in all. This sample shows the business side of the practice only: scheduling, billing and claims, referrals and staffing. The clinical record is not connected.

questions.ask: How do days in A/R and the claim denial rate compare with last month?
questions.reply: Days in A/R went from 22.5 at the end of October to 19.2 at the end of November, and the denial rate from 5.9 to 6.1 percent of claims remitted. Days in A/R is the A/R at month end divided by the average daily gross charges over the 90 days before it; the denial rate is the claims denied over the claims remitted that month. questions.ask: What does our procedure say about working a denied claim?
questions.reply: Every denied claim is worked by its reason within five working days of the payer's response, by the biller it is assigned to. A missing information denial is corrected and resubmitted, or appealed if the information was on the original claim; for a member eligibility denial the biller verifies coverage, then resubmits to the right payer or bills the patient if there is no coverage; a duplicate claim denial needs no rework once the original is paid; and per our contract with the payer, a timely filing denial is not billed to the patient and goes for a write-off. The section from our billing procedure is shown above.
questions.before: Finding the practice's own procedure meant knowing which document to open, or asking the person who wrote it.
questions.now: The answer comes from the practice's own billing procedure, with the section shown.

result.query: denied claim denial worked reason rework corrected resubmitted

results.heading: Denied claims
results.text:
## Denied claims

Every denied claim is worked by its reason within five working days of the payer's response, by the biller it is assigned to, who records each step on the claim. A missing information denial is corrected and resubmitted, or appealed if the information was on the original claim. For a member eligibility denial, the biller verifies coverage, then resubmits to the right payer, or bills the patient if there is no coverage. A duplicate claim denial needs no rework once the original claim has been paid. Per our contract with the payer, a timely filing denial is not billed to the patient, so the claim goes for a write-off. A claim the payer has not decided 30 days after it was sent is followed up with the payer every 30 days. The billing lead reviews the open denials each week.

results.heading: Sending claims
results.text:
## Sending claims

The claim for each completed visit goes to the payer through the clearinghouse within two working days of the visit. A claim that is missing information is held, with the reason recorded on the claim, until the information comes in. Each payer's filing limit is in its contract with the practice. The billing lead reviews held claims at the start of each month and asks the patient again for anything still missing; a claim whose information comes in after the payer's limit can be denied for timely filing.

results.heading: Copays and patient balances
results.text:
## Copays and patient balances

Copays are collected at check-in. Once the payer has decided a claim, anything else the patient owes goes on a statement. Statements go out on the first working day of each week for balances posted the week before. A balance still owed a month after its first statement gets a second statement, and a month after that a third. After the third statement, the billing lead reviews the account and calls the patient to agree how it will be paid.
